data.claim: The gate-status why-note assembly (_why_notes/_queued_notes) lives in ddflow/services/metrics/queued.py, the only metrics module importing the gates package, while gates.outcomes imports metrics back: a two-way dependency between packages
data.falsifier: An AST scan of ddflow/services/metrics/ finds no import whose first segment is 'gates', and ddflow/services/gates/status_notes.py exists
data.mechanism: gates/outcomes.py imports ..metrics.queued at module level; metrics/queued.py imports ..gates.reasons at module level

chunk_findings.detail: The “metrics never imports gates” guard is incomplete: it only flags relative `ImportFrom` nodes whose dotted module begins with `gates`. A metrics module can still import gates and the test will pass, e.g. `from ddflow.services.gates.reasons import _unavailable_reasons` (absolute import, `node.level == 0`) or `from .. import gates` (`node.module is None`). Thus the regression test does not actually enforce the stated invariant; a future metrics-to-gates dependency can be introduced without failing this test.
